H3 cells as 64-bit integers, printed as hex

Source: R/h3-type.R
rcs_h3.Rd

Cells read from a store (h3, h3_main, h3_p<r> and any column written as rcs_h3) have class rcs_h3: a bit64::integer64 vector holding the same 64 bits that Parquet stores, sorts and filters, printed (console, tibble, sf) as the 15-character lower-case hex string that other H3 tools use.

  • Comparison, arithmetic, sorting and joins are those of integer64; joining an rcs_h3 column with an integer64 column works and gives rcs_h3 (also with dplyr::bind_rows() and vctrs::vec_c()).

  • Subsetting, c(), rep(), unique(), sort() and rev() keep the class.

  • format() and printing show NA as NA and a value that is not a valid cell as <invalid>; they never fail.

  • as.character() gives decimal strings, exactly as for integer64; use rcs_h3_hex() for hex strings.

  • A column of class rcs_h3 is stored as a 64-bit integer, like an integer64 column; class(x) <- "integer64" or bit64::as.integer64() drops the class.

  • Inside DuckDB cells stay 64-bit integers (BIGINT); the SQL macro rcs_h3_hex() of connections prepared by store_duckdb() gives their hex strings. collect() of a table opened with store_open(engine = "duckdb") gives rcs_h3 again; a dplyr::tbl() on a view of store_duckdb() is collected by dbplyr and does not. Data read by other tools, or by such a tbl(), get the class back with store_restore_types().

See also

rcs_h3_hex(), store_h3_hex(), store_restore_types(); vignette("geospatial").

Examples

cells <- bit64::as.integer64(c("599686042433355775", "599686030622195711"))
rcs_h3_hex(cells)
#> [1] "85283473fffffff" "85283447fffffff"
